title: Urbex: ‘Het Winkeltje’ in Belgium
original_text:
Het Winkeltjes (The little shop) is a well known urbex location in Belgium. Also one of the more interesting ones, as it contains a house above a small shop that still has some inventory left
The shop is adjacent to the road, but all the windows and doors are barred. We had to climb over a wall in plain sight, which wasn’t easy but we managed to do it. Only to discover that it was possible to simply walk around that wall. Entry is not so difficult. If you know where to go.
Once we were inside, we unfortunately had to conclude that this shop has been raided quite a bit now. But it is still clearly a shop and with the right angles I managed to take some nice shots.
Above the shop there is a house which is unfortuntaly trashed even more. We are glad that we visited Het Winkeltje now, because probably in a few months nothing really interesting will be left here.

title: Urbex: Ferme Aux Drapeaux in Belgium
original_text:
The urbex trip to Belgium brought me to Ferme Aux Drapeaux. The second location we visited after Maison Milka was really breathtaking. A big farm with as a bonus a blue camper van in the shed.
Ferme Aux Drapeaux is easily accessible via the back and is a big building with a courtyard. The house is has some great authentic details. Particularly the doors are memorable. The living room has flags on the walls which is why the locations is called “Ferme Aux Drapeaux” which translates as “Flag Farm”.
The camper van is a great bonus within this location. We actually almost missed it! It is a B1000 Barkas, built in communist East Germany during the cold war. One wonders why this fascinating vehicle is now left to rot in an abandoned farm in Belgium.
We encountered another couple doing urbex photography. This urbex location seems to be quite popular at the moment but that is no surprise at is well worth it.
In the stables we found a dead cat, it looked like it was mummified!

title: Urbex: Maison Milka in Belgium
original_text:
Doing urbex photography has always been one of my bucket list items. How fitting to do this after the Covid lockdown limited by photography activities for over a year. I went to Belgium and visited various worthwhile locations.
First one I visited is called ‘Maison Milka’. An ordinary house in an ordinary street that from a distance doesn’t look all that deserted. Entrance is gained through the back. Inside, the house is unfortunately a bit trashed already. But the attic in particular is still interesting. Beware of the smell though.

title: Tel Aviv and Jerusalem
original_text:
During a business trip I visited Tel Aviv and Jerusalem in Israel. Tel Aviv is right at the Mediterranean, and Jerusalem is a 3000 year old holy city. A perfect opportunity for some photography!
In Tel Aviv I managed to capture a sunset at the beach. It was quite nice as there was a lot of color in the sky.
In Jerusalem we walked the path that Jesus took with the cross, from the mount of Olives onto the Vila Rosa.

title: The Julian Alps in Slovenia
original_text:
In Slovenia’s Triglav National Park there are so many enchanting places. When we were in The Julian Alps, we did not only find churces, waterfalls or gorges but also several other landscapes that we couldn’t resist to photograph.
The source of the Save river for example, is such a postcard place that you just can’t believe it to be true. The water there is super clear while you can see vulcanic activity going on in the pond. 
When you have Lake Bled, it is tempting to stay there and not venture further. But less than an hour’s drive from Lake Bled, you will find Lake Bohinj. While there is no church on an island in the middle, this is also a beautiful clear lake within the mountains.
And let’s not forget the countryside. Everywhere the grass looks like it was cut with the greatest precision. Even though you are in the middle of nowhere. There are forests everywhere. We even went to see brown bears that are living there, but unfortunately they did not show up.

title: Gorges of Slovenia
original_text:
In the Julian Alps you have some spectacular gorges. We visited two of them: Vintgar Gorge and Tolmin Gorge. Both very beautiful in their own way.
The trail along Vintgar Gorge is just stunning to do. But be early. We were there just when it opened and it allowed us around 30 minutes of time to photograph the gorge without many people walking the trail. But afterwards it became very busy.
Tolmin is less spectacular maybe, but has a lot more places that can be discovered. It is not one path that everyone has to take, so there is more space between the visitors. We also enjoyed Tolmin, though I must admit nothing beats Vintgar.

title: Waterfalls of Slovenia
original_text:
The Julian Alps in Slovenia are magnificent. We visited Triglav National Park. There are some exceptional waterfalls here that each have their own unique beauty.
Places we visited are Slap Peričnik, Slap Savica, Slap Peračica, Slap Boka, Slap Kozjak and Slap Grmečica. Each site was special in its own way. We were not in the right season though. It was quite hot and the waterfalls were smaller than in other times of the year. 
If we return to Slovenia, we would pick spring for example, when melting snow from the mountains will cause the waterfalls to be much bigger. But even now it was fantastic to visit some of these remarkable places.

title: Churches of Slovenia
original_text:
They are everywhere in Slovenia’s beautiful countryside: small white churches. Often built on hilltops, they are a beautiful part of the landscape.
When we visited Slovenia, we made sure to visit as many of these picturesque churches as we could. We visited sites like Sveti Tomaž, Sveti Jacob, Sv. Peter nad Begunjami and St. Primoz. And of course Bled.
But not only did we visit well known locations, but sometimes we stopped at a church along the road, without even knowing its name.

title: Lake Bled, Slovenia
original_text:
Lake Bled is one of those places you see on a postcard and think: this must be on the other side of the world. That’s far from the truth in this case, Lake Bled is in Slovenia.
The lake is beautiful for many reasons. The water is crystal clear. The location is stunning surrounded by mountains. And last but not least, there is a small island in the middle with a distinct white church on it.
This is one of these fairytale locations any photographer wants to visit.
We were there in the summer so the lake was quite busy. But from a high viewpoint this was barely noticable. We climbed the two viewpoints Ojstrica and Mala Osojnica. Also we returned to the lake in the evening to do a shoot during sunset.

title: Lohagad Fort near Pune, India
original_text:
I stayed in Pune, India for work and did not want to miss the opportunity to go out on a trek to see some of the incredible nature. Lohagad fort is one of those awe inspiring places you’d normally see on the cover of a travel magazine.
To reach Lohagad, we had to get out of the city early. We left at 5am in the morning, to avoid the chaotic traffic of the city of Pune and to be able to do the climb in relative moderate weather. Monsoon season was slowly starting up, but there was no assurance of refreshing rain.
On the way up, our car nearly broke down, but luckily we were able to get to our destination with some pushing and praying. In the village we were welcomed by some monkeys. Quite a few of their relatives manned the fort we learned, as we ascended.
Lohagad fort even has a ‘Monkey Gate’ now, revealing a room full of monkeys ready to steal your bag or even the glasses from your face. We ware advised not to open anything and keep a close watch on our belongings. Not an easy task when you’re also climbing centuries old slippery steps in the mountains.
Once we were in the fort, the views were amazing. Not only of the surroundings but also the fort itself, which stretches out over the whole mountain. It must have been so hard to build this, let alone conquer it. Later in monsoon season, the fort colors all green. Now it was mostly brown and grey, but still by all means a worthy site.

title: De Terp van Leidschenveen
original_text:
De Terp is a location just 10 minutes drive from my home town, in Leidschenveen. It looks like a small church or chapel but in fact is a work of art erected in 2009.
De Terp is an amazing place. The green hill with the white building on top could just as easily have been in Scandinavia, or could have been used in a Tolkien movie. Amazing, and right here in Holland. 
The building is not a church. There are no religious signs on it. It’s also much smaller than it seems from a distance. 
The site was designed by architect Laurens Kolks, who did a remarkable job in my opinion.
Surrounding the chapel is an ordinary urban area. People come here for a short walk with their dog. Even though it is between my home town Zoetermeer and The Hague, I did not know before this place existed. So it was kind of a nice surprise to find it.

title: Dubai Atlantis and Jumeirah from The Palm
original_text:
Breathtaking views from The Palm Dubai towards the Jumeirah coastline and Atlantis Hotel. Our visit to Dubai in 2019 was a memorable one. Not only did we enjoy a great stay in Fairmont The Palm Hotel, but I also had the opportunity to be at two beautiful photo locations. The first viewpoint on Jumeirah is from the hotel’s private beach.
The second one featuring Atlantis Hotel is from The Pointe, a new beachfront destination. Probably the best place to photograph this outlandish hotel.

title: Meijendel Beach
original_text:
Meijendel nature reserve is one of those places I keep coming back to. It is a remarkable combination of forests, dunes and beach to explore.
In the cold February month, Meijendel is less busy. I was there with my son (5) who followed me through the rough terrain without any complaints at all.
We arrived at the beach around sunset, so it was a perfect opportunity to take some photos there. On the beach we even discovered a quite rare find. Hundreds of starfishes were stranded on the beach. We had to be careful not to step on them.
To view other photos I made in Meijendel, covering forest and dunes, please check out my previous Meijendel shoots.
Meijendel, October 2016
Meijendel, December 2016

title: Budapest Parliament
original_text:
My final post with photos from the wonderful trip I made to Budapest earlier this year. There is one location there that you simple can’t skip for an awesome photo and that’s the parliament building. It is an impressive building by itself, but in the evening it is even more stunning as it is magically lit.
The Hungarian parliament is in the heart of the city, so you can’t miss it. The most common shot to take is straight from the other side of the river. What makes it challenging is that there are a lot of boats on the river blocking the view. Especially one ship that was docked in front of it, making it impossible to take the shot as we wanted.
It seemed we would not be able to take the photo. But we were lucky. just before we left, we tried the location again and the ship was away. We immediately took advantage of it. Just a few minutes later, the ship already came back and the view was blocked again.
The reflection in the river is so intense, it looks like pure gold.
It’s not on this photo, but in the sky above the building we could see small lights, like falling stars or fireflies. But at that distance it would not be possible to see flies. It turns out that it are actually birds that are lit up by the bright lights of the building!

title: Mushrooms in Mastbos Forest
original_text:
The Mastbos forest is the oldest forest in The Netherlands. It is next to the city of Breda and a wonderful area for a hike. Here we went around autumn and found some of the most perfect mushrooms you can find.
It was a bit difficult to get photos from the forest itself, because there was a lot of lumber jacking going on. Trees were cut down and piled up. Also the autumn colors were not at their height when we visited the forest.
But the mushrooms we found clearly made up for it. There were some beautiful fly agaric mushrooms that were just perfect.
Also the 15th century Castle of Bouvigne, which is right next to the forest, was pretty awesome to behold during blue hour.

title: Budapest Metro
original_text:
While Budapest is absolutely stunning above ground, one should not overlook the metro system in this city. There are a couple of metro stations that are beautifully made. 
We had quite a challenge photographing these places. Not only because of the constant flow of travelers passing by, but also because of the security guards. For some reason, they were very annoyed by us making photographs. We were not allowed to use a tripod and they watched our every move, as if we were planning something devious. Honestly I don’t understand what is so suspicious about photography.
Luckily we got the shots we were hoping for in the end.
What’s interesting about the metrostations is that they are a reflection of the time they were built. Also, the old carts are still running on the older lines. In this way it is very harmonious together.

title: Fisherman’s Bastion in Budapest
original_text:
The Fisherman’s Bastion in Budapest is one of those places that I just had to visit. A fairytale-like castle on a hill in the heart of the city, with breathtaking views.
The Fisherman’s Bastion (Halaszbastya, Budapest) was built from 1895 to 1902. It is one of the top tourist attractions of the city. It is no question why. The fortifications were built to spice up the cathedral that is also on the hill and it just looks gorgeous, right out of a Tolkien book.
Of course this was a prime target for us to photograph. But the crowds were a major difficulty here. Most photos taken from Fisherman’s Bastion are taken in winter, when it is much more quiet. 
We had to be very patient. Late in the evening we got what we came for, at least on some locations. Of course by then it was already dark, so no blue hour shots unfortunately. But even so, the night shots are still equally stunning.

title: Bridges of Budapest
original_text:
I made a citytrip to Budapest in September. Budapest is a wonderful city with plenty of opportunities for photography. In a way it is an undiscovered gem in Europe. There are so many impressive buildings there, it is really amazing for Hungary which is a country of less than 10 million people.
The city is composed of two merged cities: Buda and Pest, with the Danube river running through them. The bridges of Budapest, especially the historic ones, are truly magnificent. The steel Margareth bridge not only connects the two sides of the river, but also the island in the middle.
The chain bridge or Széchenyi lánchíd, is also grandiose. It is beautifully illuminated during the evening. During world war II all bridges were destroyed by the Germans, but wonderfully restored.

title: Interesting Staircases in Paris and Rome
original_text:
I have made several city trips in Europe last month, e.g. to Paris and Rome. In both cities, my time for photography was very limited. Luckily, the hotels I stayed in provided an unexpected opportunity: their staircases.
The hotel I stayed in Paris was in a classic building, and contains a classic spiral staircase made of wood.
In Rome I stayed in The Hive, which is a brand new hotel in the city’s center. It houses in one of the few modern buildings you can find there and has a very different staircase. But it is equally interesting, especially because of the reflection that continues the pattern of the stairs on the floor.
I love to find unexpected surprises like this. This is why I always bring my Sony RX100-III camera. It is very small and the quality is outstanding for such a small device.

title: The Atlantic Coast of Northern Portugal
original_text:
I stayed two weeks in the north of Portugal in the vicinity of the city of Porto. The coast there is amazing, with sandy beaches and rocky formations everywhere. I took some photographs here during sunset, mainly in the area between the village of Espinho and the Capela do Sinhor da Pedra.
What is awesome about this beach area, is that there is a long wooden path that you can take along the shores. This is used a lot by runners and pedestrians. During the evening it is very quiet. I enjoyed walking here a lot.

title: Capela do Senhor da Pedra
original_text:
During my stay in the North of Portugal, I came across this beautiful chapel built on the beach. The Capela do Senhor da Pedra is a magical place.
A chapel built on a few large rocks, so close to the sea. At sunset you can almost feel the divine presence there.
I took several photos there during a marvelous sunset. The chapel is popular among tourists, but luckily they only visit in large numbers during the day. I tried different angles. The beach itself here is also very interesting, with its beautifully shaped rocks lying everywhere.
The chapel is well worth a visit if you’re in the vicinity of Porto, especially if you realize it’s just a 15 minute drive away.

title: Industrial Bloodmoon
original_text:
A red ‘blood moon’ could be viewed last night. I photographed it at the Boels site near my house in Zoetermeer, to create an industrial atmosphere.
Due to thick clouds the blood moon was only visible a few minutes on my location. Unfortunately I was unable to get a super sharp picture. But the one I have, demonstrates the idea I had with it, picturing the moon inside the basket of the machine.

title: Dragonflies at Oisterwijk
original_text:
On the way back from a short weekend in Eindhoven, we stopped at Oisterwijk to explore the forest there. Natuurmonumenten has created and preserved some wonderful areas there, with trees and small ponds that are popular fishing spots.
When we wandered through the marvelous forest, we spotted whole swarms of colorful dragonflies. I had to try to photograph some of them, which was not easy because they don’t pause for long. But I managed to spot a blue one and a red one resting on a leaf.

title: Zoetermeer Dobbe
original_text:
For an upcoming InstaWalk event in my home town Zoetermeer, I want to take some photos on locations that we will probably visit. On of these locations is the Dobbe, right in the center of the city, near the market square and city hall.
The Dobbe is not a super inspiring place, but it has its charm. Certainly around sunset. There is a very nice restaurant there called Bo & Ro, that I would recommend to anyone looking for a nice place to eat in Zoetermeer.
In the water there is some art which can look nice with its reflection in the water. Also a new wooden bridge better connects the old village with the new city center. There is a small park with trees on the other side, which provides a nice view over the lake.
The sky was pretty interesting that evening. One issue with the location is that there is a lot of construction going on. I should return here at a later stage when it is all done.

title: Visit to Dublin City Center and Citywest
original_text:
During a short business visit in Dublin, I explored city center. It is an amazing city with a lot of history.
The city is built along the Liffey river, with a lot of bridges to cross it. The weather is seldom very good, so the surroundings always seem to have a bit of a grim look to it, which you may like or not. Poverty has been common in Ireland for a long time. There has been a ‘Great Famine’ in 1840 which killed more than a million Irish and accelerated the diaspora of millions more. In the city there are plenty of places that remind of these times. But there’s also a lot of new or refurbished buildings from big tech companies like Google and Facebook. A city with a lot of faces.
The little time I had, I walked along the Liffey river. We also stayed in the Citywest area and visited the DCU Ryan Academy. This building is very peculiarly shaped like two hatched eggs. I couldn’t resist applying some HDR effects on this.
NOTE: The photo from DCU Ryan Academy was taken with permission of the academy

title: Night in Amsterdam
original_text:
Amsterdam is a beautiful city and it is practically around the corner for me. That’s why I decided to go there and take some pictures on the most famous locations.
For some reason I’m not a frequent visitor of our capital. It is usually very crowded and I find in general people are not that nice. Most of the time you are addressed in English instead of your own language. But I have to admit that the city is very beautiful. 
So armed with a camera we made the trip to Amsterdam, using the excellent Park & Ride system. We drove to the Amsterdam Arena and took a metro there to the city center. An easy and cheap way to visit Amsterdam, which is hell otherwise if you drive there by car.
We first scouted the area and it was clear that we were not the only ones taking pictures of the city. On the prime spot at the canals there was a whole pack of photographers present. We even had to move to a different perspective, because there was no space. To make sure we would have a spot, we set up shop there an hour before sunset. 
A lot of passing pedestrians asked me why there were so many photographers there. People thought that some celebrity was coming or something. I explained that we all wanted to photograph the same bridges there. A bit silly if you put it like that.
It was kind of a disaster to photograph there, because of the weather there were a lot of boats on the canals. I managed to take only a handfull of decent shots in over an hour. The rest of the photographers must have been equally frustrated. Most of them remained even after we left. Probably waiting for that one minute no boats were in sight.
On the way back we stopped at the Damrak, where there is also a very nice view over the water.

title: Mandelabrug Zoetermeer Photos
original_text:
The “Nelson Mandelabrug” or Mandela Bridge is one of Zoetermeer’s most iconic landmarks. It spans the A12 motorway and features a railway station in the middle. There is a cycling path in the bridge. 
I don’t consider the Mandelabridge to be an impressive bridge in any way, but it is hard to miss when you are driving on the A12 highway towards The Hague. The blue and yellow colors of the bridge are the colors of the municipality. I took my photos in black & white because I personally don’t like the colors very much, but I left one photo in (toned down) colors you can see how it is supposed to look.
The light and many leading lines inside of the bridge make it an interesting photography object. With all the signs, trash cans and people it is quite challenging, but as Zoetermeer is my home town, this location was was a must visit for me. Hope you enjoy my work.

title: Riverland Dubai
original_text:
I have visited Dubai a couple of times and everytime it presents new photo opportunities. This time I went to Riverland in Dubai Parks & Resorts.
Riverland is an interesting place. It connects all the themeparks of Dubai Parks & Resorts, and is kind of a themepark itself. There are restaurants and bars. The whole mood is that of an old European city. In the evening it is very nice to walk there and have a bite in one of the venues.
When I was taking photos there, I was stopped by a security official. Apparently it is not allowed to use a tripod and photograph the area. Weird, but true. Luckily I had already made some shots before I had to put away my gear.

title: La Mer in Dubai
original_text:
In March I spent some time in Dubai, UAE. This city never ceases to amaze me. A completely new beachfront area has been opened: La Mer. 
La Mer is beautifully designed. The beach is nice but the area around has also been transformed to become one of the hottest places in the city. For a drink or dinner, you can choose from a variety of restaurants and bars. La Mer is not fully completed, but what’s there already attracts a lot of people. 
Things that caught my attention are the fake tram rails in the urban area and the colorful cabins in the beach area.
La Mer has been developed by a company called Meraas, that has also been the developer of some other new hot locations in Dubai, such as The Walk, City Walk and Box Park.

title: Maasvlakte Rotterdam Industrial Photos
original_text:
The Maasvlakte is a huge artificial landmass near Rotterdam, where ships unload their cargo and factories process them. The building I photographed there is the Lyondell Chemical Plant.
It had been on my list for quite a while to drive to the Maasvlakte and take photos there. But being an industrial site, it is quite hard to find places that are suitable for a photo. Most interesting plants are blocked by fences, wires, buildings, piles of sand or simply impossible to reach. Lyondell Chemical Plant is fortunately an exception. Not the biggest plant in the area, but certainly one of the more interesting ones. 
Visitors are warned however not to come too close, as the ground surrounding the factory is full of ‘dangerous pipes’ as the signs around the plant claim. We did not test this and remained at a safe distance. Luckily I had a lens with me capable of zooming in a little on the action.
I always find it curious how plants like this get built. It seems every pipe and tower has just grown on top of it, like it is alive somehow. There seems to be no system in it at all.
It was extremely cold and the wind was very powerful, making it difficult to get a sharp shot without movement, especially since I shot this one bracketed for HDR processing.

title: Oosterheem Zoetermeer in Winter
original_text:
On a cold winter day I took some pictures in Oosterheem, Zoetermeer. The water was party frozen and there was a nice sunset.
For a few days it has been unusually cold in The Netherlands. Because of the strong winds, it took a long time for the water to freeze, but now the ice is thick enough in some places for ice-skating. This always lifts the spirits in The Netherlands and people venture onto the ice in great numbers.
In Oosterheem Zoetermeer, there is a nice canal which was party frozen. This is a suitable spot for a nice photo with reflections during blue hour.
I also visited the Bentwoud, which is a man made forest. Although the trees are still so small, it doesn’t deserve the name yet. The Bentwoud is on the edge of Zoetermeer and here I was alone with pheasants and rabbits. On of the rodents had been slain, its skeleton head still lying around. Which provided a nice foreground for one of my pictures.

title: Watertoren Zoetermeer
original_text:
The water tower in Zoetermeer is a structure built in 1927. It is one of the few buildings from a time when Zoetermeer was only a small town. 
The water tower in Zoetermeer was designed by architect C. Visser from Delft and was built 1927-1928. The tower has a height of 48,65 meters and one watercontainer of 500 m³. It is called “De Tien Gemeenten”.
I have been here before in 2015, but then it was a rainy day and I did not have a full frame camera yet. Now the sky was clear and I had the Sony A7R2 with a Zeiss 16-35mm lens at my disposal.
Yet it is not the easiest spot to take a good photo. The few good viewpoints I could find were blocked by bushes or otherwise not working out as I hoped. In the end I ended up with the same compositions as before. But because the weather was very different the photos do have a very different look.

images.alt: Water Tower with water in front

title: Urbex in Zoetermeer
original_text:
Doing some Urban Exploration (urbex) was on my bucket list for some time. So it was a golden opportunity when an office building just a block away from my house was being demolished.
The building, right behind the showroom of the defunct Impala cardealer in Zoetermeer, had already been deserted for some time. I was not surprised it was now finally being torn down. However this was happening so quickly that I had to hurry not to miss this opportunity. Only half the structure was still standing when we entered it.
Unfortunately, most of the interesting details were already gone, but strangely enough we discovered that there were a couple of broken bicycles lying around in the building. This offered as a nice foreground for one of the pictures.
It had also rained quite a bit and because the windows and parts of the ceiling were gone this resulted in a lot of standing water on the floor, providing some nice reflections.
Photomatix
I shot these images with the Sony 16-35 Zeiss lens on a bracketed setting and postprocessed them using the excellent Photomatix Pro, which allows for the dramatized effect you see in these photos.
I’m quite happy with the result. It is not an abandoned nuclear plant, hospital or theater, but for Zoetermeer the urbex options are limited. A sign that says “keep this room clean” in Dutch was a hilarious detail I discovered in the hallway full of debris.

title: The Spanish Towers on Sardinia
original_text:
When I was in Sardinia earlier this year, I found that the beautiful coastline was even more interesting because of the so called ‘Spanish Towers’. I photographed one of these towers in the south. 
The Spanish Towers are structures built along the coast in the days of the Aragon empire, to defend Sardinia against frequent raids and attacks from the Arabs. Whenever ships were spotted they could warn the population in advance. Many of these towers are still landmarks along the coast and have given their name to the nearby beaches or villages.
They can be found all around Sardinia and date centuries back, but they are not thousands of years old, such as the world famous ‘Muraghe’ inland, and therefore don’t get as much attention. But they should, because they have a unique positioning, overseeing bays on strategic places.
It required a lot of scouting until I found interesting compositions to picture this tower, because I wanted its majestic beauty to shine through on the photograph. I think I eventually did succeeded. Especially after sunset the tower really becomes one with the surrounding landscape.

title: Autumn Colors in Kaapse Bossen
original_text:
The Kaapse Bossen are one of the most beautiful forests in The Netherlands. Famous for its autumn colors. This year I made a long walk through the forest, capturing as much of the colorful beauty as I could.
Kaapse Bossen is a nature reserve in the Utrecht province, being managed by Natuurmonumenten. Hendrik Swellengrebel bought the area around 1750, after returning from South-African Capetown. The forests reminded him of the forest behind the Table Mountain near Capetown. Amidst the Kaapse Bossen is the estate De Ruiterberg. The gardens of this estate were created between 1917 and 1923, by garden architect Petrus Hermannus Wattez.
It was actually pretty busy in the forest with people, as the weather was very good for this time of year. It took some time to shoot these photos without people on them. I made most shots with the 24-240 Sony lens, leveraging the compression achieved when zooming in on the trees. There were also some typical mushrooms on the ground, and I did not forget about those.

title: Texel’s Beautiful Lighthouse
original_text:
The lighthouse on the island of Texel, Netherlands. Texel is Holand’s biggest island, bordering on one side the Northern Sea and on the other side the Waddenzee.
The lighthouse is very iconic. It was built in 1864. At the end of WW2 it was destroyed and rebuilt.
A nice fact about the Texel lighthouse, is that a very similar one can be found on the other side of the world, on the small island of Pulau Breueh, Indonesia. That is called the Willemstoren and was built by the Dutch in the colonial era. It is also still being operated today.
I shot these pictures during a weekend on the island. It was raining all the time, so it was difficult to find a moment to take out the camera. Even worse, I forgot to bring my tripod, so I could not make any long exposures. But nevertheless I am quite happy with the results. The road towards the lighthouse acts as a very nice leading line and the colors in the sky were awesome.

title: Capo Spartivento on Sardinia
original_text:
I visited Sardinia for a short holiday and used the opportunity to photograph its beautiful shorelines. 
One of the most enchanting places I found in South-Sardinia in the province of Cagliari is called Capo Spartivento. There is a lighthouse there (Faro Capo Spartivento) dating back to 1866. The water is crystal clear and the rocky bay is just stunningly beautiful.
When I arrived on the spot there was a boat there with people snorkling, so I had to wait quite a while in the burning sun to be able to take shots without the boat.
I did not use a filter, but I simulated the long exposures with the excellent Sony Smooth Reflections app. This way I could shoot up to 128 photos that compose a single image, smoothing the water.
Enjoy these photos. I’ll post more of my trip to Sardinia in the coming weeks.

title: Zaanse Schans
original_text:
The Zaanse Schans is one of Holland’s most popular tourist attractions. A village full of typically Dutch farms and windmills. We ventured there to shoot some classic Dutch landscape photos.
We arrived around 15:00 on the scene. Of course during the day, there are a lot of tourists here. It’s impossible to photograph anything without 300 Chinese in front of your lens making selfies. But we were not here to shoot photos, yet. Instead we scouted the area and looked for the best places to go to around sunset.
The buildings close at 18:00 hours. After that it is much more quiet and peaceful on the Zaanse Schans. I recommend anyone who wants to visit this place to go around this time. All the buses of annoying people are gone and the experience of the area is so much better. Ok, the mills, shops and museums are closed. But that’s a small price to pay. So now we were able to wander around freely and photograph the beautiful landscape. It was extra quiet because we had a little bit of rain. Not too much luckily, but just enough to scare away any remaining tourists.
Most of the buildings at the Zaanse Schans were not originally situated there. In the late 60’s they were moved to this location, to preserve them in an open air museum village. There is no fee to enter Zaanse Schans. The houses are occupied with residents, so it is not only tourists wandering around.
It was actually pretty hard to find good spots for photographs around this time of year. The water was dirty with crush and plants, sometimes they were entirely green, with no reflections left.
We focused on some of the more well known spots, the mills along the water and the farm with the nice bridge in the front. I think it worked out quite well. The original idea was to come back the next morning very early. But we were satisfied with this session, so we skipped that plan in favor of some extra sleep and a nice breakfast at the Van Der Valk hotel we were staying in.

title: Eendrachtsmolen and Rottemeren Photos
original_text:
The Rottemeren are just 15 minutes drive from my home. The area consists of a few lakes that are connected by the river Rotte. There is also a mill there, known as the “Eendrachtsmolen”.
When we parked our car, we discovered that the mill is on the other side of the lake. To reach it, we had to walk around it, which was a nice but long walk. But in the end, it was worth it. The pictures of the mill, with the traditional Dutch surroundings, are very nice and there is a typical waterlock nearby. The only minor drawback of the location are the countless signs everywhere.

title: A peaceful look over Sweet Lake
original_text:
The Noord-AA lake near my home town Zoetermeer (Sweet Lake City) is one of my favorite spots. A very simple composition, but combined with a long exposure effect I managed to achieve a soothing image.
My regular spot near the pier was taken and there was too much wind to be able to shoot there. I decided to drive around the lake and see if there were any other worthwhile spots to be found. It was very crowded because it was a warm day, so I nearly gave up. Until I found this empty steel bench. It was interesting enough to become my foreground, while the background did not contain any buildings or people.
There was not much reflection in the water and the sunset was also not in the picture, but using the long exposure effect that the Sony camera provides, with the ‘reflections’-app, I was able to create an interesting photo nonetheless. I like the black & white version best.

title: Vlietlanden Long Exposures
original_text:
I wanted to take some long exposure shots with reflection in the water. There are a couple of options near Zoetermeer. This time I chose the Vlietlanden, an area close to Voorschoten just a few minutes drive.
At first I wanted to go to the Noord-AA, but it was so crowded that I decided to go a bit further. The Vlietlanden area are partly under construction, so it was very quiet there. Although it was not easy to find an interesting spot.
Finally I managed to find a viewpoint that had enough interesting elements to use in a photo. I took a few long exposures here to make the water nice and flat. There is also a special app of the A7R camera that allows ‘smooth reflections’. This worked remarkably well. Although I learned that this feature is best used when it is not very dark. Otherwise it will take a lot of time.

title: Zeeland and Zierikzee Photoshoot
original_text:
I visited Zeeland last weekend, and the city of Zierikzee in particular. Zeeland is a remarkable province in Holland. It is flat and quiet. And it has a long history of struggle with the sea. Now it is a popular holiday destination for the Dutch and the Germans.
The last major flooding of Zeeland was in 1953. After this ‘great flood’, the ambitious ‘delta’ project was initiated by the Dutch government, to prevent future floodings. A lot of dams, dykes and constructions were built all over the province the following decade. Since then, the country has changed a lot and is safe from the sea.
The city of Zierikzee is one of the most remarkable I have ever visited. It is very old, with the oldest buildings still standing dating back to the 15th century. It has more than 500 official monuments, which is a lot for a city with only about 11.000 inhabitants.
Near Zierikzee you can also find the Zeeland bridge. This bridge over the Eastern Scheldt is more than 5 kilometers long. When it was opened, it was the longest bridge in Europe and it is still the longest bridge of The Netherlands. It has a certain elegance to it that I like.
Aside from Zierikzee, I also visited the Plompe Toren in Kouwekerke. This town does no longer exist, because it was consumed by the sea in 1700. The church tower was spared and still stands there as a reminder of the devastating powers of the sea. The city sign of Kouwekerke is also still present, making this formally the smallest Dutch town, with zero inhabitants.

title: Old Carwreck
original_text:
Plaswijck Park is a place near Rotterdam where kids can play. My eye cought this old but fascinating carwreck standing there.
I did not have my regular A7RII camera with me, so I used the more portable MX100-III to take a bracketed three shots without tripod. The HDR effect was applied with Photomatix Pro. Sometimes an effect like this can be too much, but for this particular photo I think it worked out very nice.

title: Wilhelminapier Rotterdam
original_text:
The Wilhelminapier is a fantastic place to be in Rotterdam. The classic Hotel New York is there to visit or you can have a bite at restaurant Las Palmas. Also the famous Erasmus Bridge can be found here.
We made a short photowalk around the Wilhelminapier. On the other side there is a nice pedestrian bridge, which also made a good foreground. Walking a bit further we found a nice spot along the Maas, to photograph the Erasmus Bridge and the Euromast. The sky was colorful and red today. Unfortunately the light was a bit less intense around the bridge, but we still managed to shoot some very nice pictures.

title: Scheveningen, Beach and Pier
original_text:
Scheveningen is the closest beach to my house. It is a really popular seaside resort and when the weather is good, it can be very crowded. I went there to take some shots from the Pier in the sea. But also the Kurhouse and Beelden aan Zee. 
First there is the sculpture Thsuki-No-Kikari near Museum Beelden aan Zee. This statue is visible from the beach of Scheveningen. Surprisingly I had not spotted it before. I like its mysterious look.

title: Noord-AA Red Sky
original_text:
The Noord-AA, or Zoetermeer lake, is the primary recreation area of the city. It is a man-made lake with depths of up to 30 meters. It is also a very nice place to be at sunset and easy to reach.
When I saw the sky turn bright red, I drove to the lake to take a few photos. I visited some spots I had used before to get the best effect possible with the amazing sky of that day. In post production the challenge was to make it look natural, because the red color is so powerful that enhancing it did not make the photo better.

title: Winterphotos of Meijendel Nature Reserve
original_text:
My second excursion to the dunes of Meijendel. Early december it is cold and the trees have lost their leaves. Sunset starts early and can be very beautiful. It gives the area a whole new look.
Meijendel is a remarkable nature reserve, because you have forest, dunes and beach in one place. This time I visited the dunes mostly. There is amazing light here, but there is little time to benefit from it. Sometimes it is hard to find good locations for a photo, because there are areas that are protected with fences and barbed wire.

title: Morning at the Rottemeren
original_text: I usually don’t photograph in the morning, but this time I made an exception. We drove to the Rottemeren, which is only 15 minutes from my home. It was a nice foggy morning. I arrived on the spot a little late. The sun was already above the horizon. But even so, the fog added a nice mood to the photos. Added benefit of the fog is that it hides some distracting elements. For example the lonely tree at the other side of the lake is not that lonely. The fog hides some ugly appartment buildings that are a little bit further away.

title: The Beauty of Meijendel, near The Hague
original_text:
If you’re looking for a unique nature reserve near the city of The Hague in The Netherlands, you don’t have to go far. Meijendel Nature Reserve offers a beautiful combination of dunes, forests and beach right around the corner. 
A wide area of dunes is needed to protect the Dutch shores against the sea. Because these dunes are needed to preserve the land, they are kept in nice condition and are a beautiful landscape to wander around.
Nature can have its way here creating fairytale-like places with trees, grass, water and all kinds of animals.
Once you’ve completed the walk through the forests and the dunes, the reward is a broad beach with the open sea right in front of you. If this story does not convince you, just have a look at the photos.

title: The Windmills of Kinderdijk
original_text:
Kinderdijk is a famous place in The Netherlands for tourists, where you have a lot of typical windmills in one place. It is also just around the corner for me. So I decided to go there and take some photos.
It was not a particularly nice day and the sky wasn’t all that interesting. But even so, the sights there are quite amazing. My best photo was selected to feature in the Holland Calendar 2017, so maybe you will see it in the bookstores soon.

title: Den Bosch
original_text: I sometimes like to go to a city, simply to look around and drink a beer or two. This time I was in Den Bosch, and I took a few shots while I was there. Of course the square was nice with all the lights. But also the waterways, with their clear reflections.

title: Meerpolder and Snow World
original_text: The Meerpolder near Zoetermeer is a unique agricultural area in the Netherlands, because it has a round shape. The big Snow World building is also next to it.The polder itself is protected, so you’ll find mostly cows and sheep there. Also it is a favorite spot for many birds, such as storks and egrets. It took me a while to discover the beauty of this place. But it is a grateful place if you have your camera with you.

title: Oostpoort Delft
original_text:
The Oostpoort (Eastern Gate) is a historical site in Delft. The gate is old, it was built around 1400. It is an example of Brick Gothic northern European architecture. Around 1510 the towers were enhanced with an additional octagonal floor and high spires. This is the only city gate remaining in Delft; the others were demolished in the 19th century. It currently serves as an art gallery and private residence.
The Oostpoort has a special meaning for me, because we made our wedding photographs here. The photographer that made them, Ralf Czogallik, is one of the best wedding photographers in The Netherlands. I knew I would not match his quality. But I went during sunset, so my photos would be very different. Unfortunately when we arrived at the location, there were three significant setbacks. First, the sky wasn’t really interesting. Second, there was a lot of green algae in the water. And third, there was construction work being done.
Nevertheless I did my best to take a few decent photos. But I certainly have to go back here again under better circumstances.

title: Noord-AA Fisherman
original_text: The second time I visited the Noord-AA lake north of my home town Zoetermeer. I went back to the same spot as last time.  There was a fisherman again and the water had a very strong golden reflection of the sun. Of course there is a little post processing done here. But most of the visible effect is because of the gradual 5-stop ND filter I used. It causes fairly strong vignetting but it also makes it possible to use long exposure times.

title: The Old City of Dordrecht and the Biesbosch
original_text:
Dordrecht, near Rotterdam, has an exceptionally beautiful city center and harbor. When we visited this city I had no trouble making some nice photos.
After visiting the city center, we rented a boat and explored the nature reserve of the ‘Biesbosch’. That was more challenging than we thought. We had a lot of trouble crossing the river with our small boat. After we reached one of the more intesting parts of the reserve, we got stuck in shallow waters. Luckily we were able to free ourselves. But it was clear that we were no born fishermen. The river delta nature reserve is beautiful and has very special islands, birds and trees.

title: The HSL High Speed Railway near Zoetermeer
original_text:
Just a few blocks away from my house, the HSL high speed railway goes past Zoetermeer. The track is nothing special at first sight, but at some points when it crosses the water it becomes very interesting on a photo. 
I imagine it must have been a weird sight when I was taking pictures of this boring concrete track. But after some retouching I am pleased with the results. In a city like Zoetermeer without an old city center, you have to get creative to find worthwhile photo locations.

title: Sunset in Oosterheem
original_text: Sometimes you don’t have to travel far for a photo. I saw nice clouds in the sky and decided to take my bike and see if I could find a good spot in my neighborhood. I found a bridge on the edge of the city. Because I did not bring my tripod, I used the edges of the bridge to steady my camera. Of course this is not a million dollar shot. But I like the composition and the reflection of the sun in the water.

title: The Pier of Scheveningen
original_text:
A visit to Scheveningen beach and the Pier, which is under construction.The Pier is a well known landmark from Scheveningen. For years it has been neglected until it almost collapsed. Now demolition and construction work is being done to restore it to its former glory.
Because it was the middle of the day, I used black & white and HDR effects to make the photos a little more interesting. I especially liked how the Bungee Jump tower turned out.

title: Haarlem and the Spaarne
original_text:
Haarlem is a beautiful city. We spent the weekend there and explored the old town. I took a few photos of Gravestenen-bridge, which is a beautiful bridge in Haarlem’s old city centre. The first photo was shot with the Sony A7RII but with an old crop lens, because I wanted to use an ND filter during golden hour. The result isn’t all that bad. Because of the filter and resulting longer shutter time, the water is nice and flat. The movement in the clouds also provides a nice effect.
The rest of the photos along the Spaarne were shot using the 28mm Sony full frame lens. As you can see, this provides a better picture overall than the Sigma 17mm crop lens. This area of Haarlem is very nice, I especially liked Teyler’s Hofje.

title: Amsterdam IJ
original_text:
After I visited Vodafone for work, I walked around the Amsterdam IJ and made some photos. I did not have a tripod and it was during daytime, so the light was nothing special. Surprisingly, the shot I made of the houseboats there became my most popular photo on 500px. 
I still wonder what makes this shot so special. I post processed it using HDR which gives a cool effect. But I also feel it is a little bit overprocessed. Clearly the photography community has a different opinion. I’ll also post an unprocessed version here, for comparison.

title: Fireworks, Happy 2016!
original_text:
I bought a new full frame camera, the Sony A7R2, to replace my aps-c Sony A77. The first time I used this camera was during new year’s eve, shooting the fireworks.
Fireworks are difficult to shoot. But I was very pleased of the quality of the images made by the A7R2. The main reason I switched cameras, was that I felt that it was the logical step to bring my image quality to the next level. Of course there is much to gain by improving my skill as well. But bringing a significantly better camera is an instant improvement, I simply couldn’t resist.
The A7R2 is an outstanding camera in many ways. It has more than twice the amount of megapixels of the A77. A much better dynamic range. It has a full frame sensor and is much smaller because it is not a true DSLR. Comparing it with Canon and Nikon options, I quickly came to the conclusion that Sony was technically the superior choice.
The only downside of the camera was that there were not that many lenses available for the new E-mount yet. This could be compensated by a A-mount converter, which I also bought. It works, but I’m not impressed by its performance. Focusing becomes a lot slower, which is undesirable for some situations. More lens options would become available in time, so I had to be patient. But the lenses that were available, are excellent quality.
For these fireworks I used the 28mm F2 lens, which has become my favorite because of its sharpness, speed, small size and all-round usable range. I took the photos from the balcony of my house.

title: Beach of Katwijk aan Zee
original_text: During Christmas we visited the beach at Katwijk aan Zee. Although there were strong winds, I managed to make some very nice photos at sunset. The beach is very beautiful at Katwijk aan Zee. I used a long exposure to get a painterly look on some of the photos.

title: Katjeskelder Mushroom
original_text:
A colorful mushroom in the forest at Katjeskelder. Katjeskelder is a resort surrounded by forests. I was there to visit my parents. I love walking through the forest. While I was walking there, I was looking to photograph some sunlight falling through to trees, but I wasn’t able to find the right composition. 
Luckily I found this colorful mushroom so I still made a nice photo on this trip.

title: Sunset at the Noord-AA
original_text:
Near Zoetermeer, there is the Noord-AA lake. It provides a retreat from the busy city for many people. Especially around sunset it can be beautiful there.
I tried different positions around the lake. There was also a fisherman. The reflections in the water are quite astonishing. I had been to this place many times without my camera, but I never noticed this before. Also I used a gradual filter for the first time, to get longer exposure times. Although there is significant vignetting because of the filter, that worked out fine for these photos.

title: Oosterheem, Zoetermeer
original_text: My neighborhood Oosterheem in Zoetermeer is very new. The shopping center was recently completed. I think they did a good job. There is a small park and a very nice canal in the middle of the area. I like to walk here after sunset, because it is very quiet. During blue hour I managed to take these photos.

title: Buytenpark Zoetermeer
original_text:
The Buytenpark in Zoetermeer is a former debris dump. But it looks a lot more friendly now. There are even Scottisch Galloways grazing there. 
I visited this park in my home town around sunset. My idea was to shoot a Galloway. Easier said than done. Of course the Galloways were not standing still all the time, so I had to follow them around a bit. Until one of them decided to graze for a while next to a pond. The moment I had been waiting for. I had to be careful though, after I took the photo the animal nearly run down me and my tripod.

title: Dutch Secret Service Building (AIVD)
original_text:
The Dutch Secret Service (AIVD) building in Zoetermeer is maybe one of the ugliest buildings in the world. Even so, it fascinates me. And because it is just arm’s length away from my office, during lunch I walked to it.
When I was right in front of the building, I did not dare to take too much time making photos. Therefore I used my small Sony RX100-III camera to make one bracketed shoot, without a tripod. 
Because most of the building is grey, I thought a strong HDR effect would give nice results in post processing. This worked out well. I think you can agree that the building on the photo does not look that ugly anymore. With some imagination, it has the looks of an advanced alien fortress.
When I was a student, I used to work here. Back then it was the Ministry of Education, where I did a holiday job. My primary task was to bring papers from one end of the building to the other; which as you can see was a good workout. There are so many hallways in this building that you can easily lose your way. Add the dislike most people have for this building and it doesn’t become strange the secret service made this their hideout.

title: Hofvijver in The Hague
original_text:
The Hofvijfer is a pond in the centre of The Hague. It is adjoined in the east by the Korte Vijverberg (road), in the south by the Binnenhof and the Mauritshuis, in the west by the Buitenhof and in the north by the Lange Vijverberg (road). In the middle there is a small island with plants and trees which has no name, it is usually referred to as “the island in the Vijverberg”.
I love coming here and walk through the “Binnenhof” where the Dutch government used to reside. The prime minister resides in “het torentje” (the small tower). The buildings give a nice reflection in the water. The photos were shot with a Sony A77 and post processed in Lightroom and Photomatix HDR.

title: Watertoren Zoetermeer
original_text:
Zoetermeer has a classic water tower. As one of the few relatively old and classic structures in the town, it is rather unique.
The water tower in Zoetermeer was designed by architect C. Visser from Delft and was built 1927-1928. The tower has a height of 48,65 meters and one watercontainer of 500 m³. I visited the tower on a rainy day, which contributes to the dark mood of my photos.
Note: I revisited this location a few years later. The weather was totally different. Check out those watertoren photos here.

title: Parking Garage Nederlandlaan Zoetermeer
original_text: The parking garage under my office was recently painted. Not that it has become that interesting. Parking garages must be among of the least inspiring places on earth. Nevertheless, I had to try some HDR. It had some rather surprising results. The HDR effect particularly works well on the colored concrete and the Tesla Model S.

title: The Mills at Zevenhuizen
original_text: Just a few minutes drive from my hometown Zoetermeer, there is a town called Zevenhuizen (seven houses) where you can find a few typical Dutch windmills. I drove here two times by bike. First on a sunny day and the second time with a clouded sky. This resulted in very different moods for both sets of photos.

title: Trip Around Iceland
original_text:
We made a trip to Iceland in the summer 2015, when it has eternal sun. Driving around the island, our primary mission was to photograph the beautiful landscape.
We saw some amazing scenery. The waterfalls are mindblowing.
What especially struck me is the emptyness of the land. In the winter it will get so cold and unhospitable that nobody wants to live here. In the summer it is still cold by European standards, but also very beautiful.
Looking back on this trip I certainly think that there are plenty of opportunities that I missed. Maybe I will go back, someday.
